linkedin.title: Most news feeds are broken because they treat everyone the same.
linkedin.body:
We all have different interests, different levels of knowledge, and different goals for our time. Yet, most platforms serve us a generic mix of popular stories that often feel irrelevant or just noisy. They prioritize what is trending over what actually matters to the individual reader.

True personalization is not just about showing you more of what you already like. It is about respecting your time. It means filtering out the clutter so you can focus on the stories that inform your specific worldview or professional needs. It is about depth over breadth.

We built Headlinne because we believe technology should act like a personal editor. It should learn what you find valuable and quietly curate the day around those priorities. When news is tailored to you, you stop skimming headlines and start actually reading.

I am curious how you currently manage your news intake. Do you feel like you are getting what you need, or are you constantly filtering out the noise yourself?

slides.subtitle: From massive chip investments to Google's hardware reveal, here is what matters.

slides.headline: Nvidia secures massive funding for AI
slides.explanation: Investors have poured 500 billion dollars into Nvidia to help build vast new data centers. This infrastructure is needed to power the massive computer chips that run modern AI systems.

slides.headline: The gap between AI hype and reality
slides.explanation: Tech executives claim AI will give employees more free time, yet staff report working up to 90 hours a week. It seems the promised work-life balance has not arrived for the people building the tech.

slides.headline: Meta tries a new AI strategy
slides.explanation: Meta is launching open AI models to try and catch up with its competitors. Mark Zuckerberg hopes this pivot will finally jumpstart the company's struggling AI efforts.

slides.headline: OpenAI fights back against cyberattacks
slides.explanation: OpenAI is releasing a new AI model specifically trained to detect and block cyberattacks. As digital threats grow, this tool aims to strengthen security defenses using automation.

slides.headline: What to watch for at Google's event
slides.explanation: Google is set to reveal its latest hardware, including new slab and foldable Pixel phones. We might also see updates to their smartwatches and new colors for their earbuds.

instagram.title: Global Updates You Should Know Today

slides.headline: Global Updates You Should Know Today
slides.subtitle: Five quick stories on the shifts shaping our world right now.

slides.headline: Ukraine Strikes Deep Inside Russia
slides.explanation: A Ukrainian drone attack hit an industrial site hundreds of miles from the border, killing at least 13 people. This marks a significant escalation in Kyiv’s strategy to target the Russian economy directly.

slides.headline: Russia Bans Anti-War Party
slides.explanation: A Moscow court ruled that the country's only liberal, anti-war party cannot run in next month's parliamentary elections. This decision effectively removes any organized political opposition from the ballot.

slides.headline: Inside Ukraine's Drone Launch Sites
slides.explanation: Journalists gained access to a secret base in eastern Ukraine where soldiers prepare long-range drones. It offers a rare look at the logistics behind the country's deep-strike capabilities.

slides.headline: Boat Operator Charged After NYC Tragedy
slides.explanation: Federal prosecutors charged a speedboat driver with misconduct after a vessel capsized in New York Harbor, killing a mother and her infant. The case highlights the serious legal consequences for negligence on the water.

slides.headline: Tech Giants Face Addiction Lawsuits
slides.explanation: A US appeals court ruled that Meta, Google, and TikTok must face lawsuits claiming their platforms are addictive. This could set a major precedent for how tech companies are held liable for user safety.
